reports.text: Left lower extremity venous duplex with compression and color Doppler. Noncompressible deep venous segment with intraluminal echogenic thrombus and absent flow, consistent with acute deep vein thrombosis. Postoperative soft tissue swelling about the knee.
reports.conclusion: Acute deep vein thrombosis, left lower extremity.

reports.text: CT pulmonary angiogram. Adequate opacification of the pulmonary arteries. Filling defect in a segmental pulmonary artery branch consistent with acute pulmonary embolus. Main and lobar pulmonary arteries patent. Heart size normal, no RV dilatation. No pleural effusion or consolidation.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 01/15/2026, arrival 08:50
Patient: Sandra Kendall, 68F
Allergies: Heparin (HIT); sulfa (rash)

CC: L calf pain and swelling

HPI: 68F POD 7 from L total knee arthroplasty (01/08/2026, this hospital system's orthopaedic service), discharged home 01/11. Two days of progressive pain and swelling of the left calf. Has been giving herself subcutaneous heparin injections twice a day since surgery per discharge orders; warfarin restarted after surgery. History of HIT with arterial thrombosis 07/2025. AF on chronic warfarin.

Meds: warfarin 5 mg, heparin 5,000 units SC q12h, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, calcium carbonate/vitamin D, acetaminophen.

Triage vitals stable. Exam: L knee incision intact with expected swelling. Left calf erythematous, warm and tender. Distal pulses present.

Labs: Hgb 13.2 g/dL, WBC 7.8 x10^9/L, platelets 55 x10^9/L (150 before surgery). PT 12 s, aPTT 35 s. D-dimer elevated.
LE venous duplex: acute DVT, left leg.

ED course: heparin stopped; hematology contacted. At 11:40, sudden shortness of breath and chest pain. BP 130/85, HR 110, SpO2 92% on room air; supplemental oxygen given. CT pulmonary angiogram: segmental PE. HIT antibody sent. Argatroban infusion started per hematology.

Impression: 1. Acute left leg DVT. 2. Acute segmental pulmonary embolism. 3. Thrombocytopenia with heparin re-exposure in patient with prior HIT - suspected recurrent HIT.

Disposition: admitted to medical ICU, 14:30.

Record faxed to PCP 01/20/2026.

events.reason: pulmonary embolism, DVT, suspected recurrent HIT

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Instructions (patient copy)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
PATIENT DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS - scanned from patient's copy at PCP visit 01/27/2026

Name: Sandra Kendall
Admitted 01/15/2026 (ICU, then medical floor). Discharged 01/22/2026.
Reason for stay: blood clot in left leg and blood clot in the lung. Low platelets from heparin (HIT). HIT antibody test: POSITIVE.

ALLERGY: HEPARIN - never receive heparin in any form (shots, IV, line flushes, enoxaparin).

In the hospital you received argatroban (IV blood thinner) and your warfarin was restarted and overlapped.
At discharge: platelets 162, INR 2.3.

Your medicines: warfarin 5 mg every evening; metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; atorvastatin 20 mg daily; calcium + vitamin D twice daily; acetaminophen as needed. STOP heparin injections.

Follow up: primary care within 1 week for INR and blood count. Orthopaedics as scheduled.
Return to the ER for chest pain, trouble breathing, new leg swelling, or bleeding.

documents.title: Outside Record Received
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record from 1/15 arrived by fax: DVT L leg and PE after knee replacement, low platelets, admitted to ICU. We had no notice of the admission. Called pt's cell, no answer, left VM. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Home From Hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I'm home since yesterday. Sorry I missed your call - I was in the hospital for a week. Clots in my leg and lung after the knee surgery, and my platelets dropped again because of heparin shots they sent me home with. I'm back on warfarin only. They said see you within a week. Sandra

documents.title: Home From Hospital - Reply
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sandra, I'm glad you're home. We have you Tuesday 1/27 at 10:00 with blood work. Please bring every paper they gave you. Go to the ER for chest pain, worse breathing or any bleeding.

events.reason: hospital follow-up: DVT, PE, HIT after left knee replacement

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Discharged 1/22. Interactive contact 1/23 via portal.

Course (ED record + her discharge instruction sheet; no discharge summary or knee surgery records received): L TKA 1/8, discharged 1/11 on warfarin plus SC heparin 5,000 units twice daily. On POD 7 to the ED with 2 days of L calf pain/swelling - DVT on duplex, platelets 55. While in the ED developed dyspnea and chest pain, CTPA segmental PE, ICU admission. HIT antibody positive. Argatroban, warfarin overlapped. Discharged on warfarin 5 mg with platelets 162 and INR 2.3.

Today: breathing back to normal, no chest pain. L calf still a bit swollen and tender but better each day. Knee stiff, doing PT exercises. No bleeding.

Exam: comfortable on room air. Irregular rhythm, rate controlled. Lungs clear. L knee incision healing, no drainage. L calf mildly swollen, minimal tenderness, no erythema.

A/P:
1. Acute L leg DVT and segmental PE, provoked (surgery), on warfarin - she stays on warfarin indefinitely for AF regardless. INR today; weekly for a month.
2. HIT, recurrent with heparin re-exposure. Platelets today to confirm recovery. Allergy prominent on chart and bracelet.
3. s/p L TKA - PT, ortho f/u.
4. Records: front desk to request discharge summary, ICU records and knee surgery op note.
5. Follow up in 4 weeks.

documents.title: CBC and INR
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Platelets 214 - recovered. INR in range. Called pt. Weekly INR x3 then spread out.

documents.title: INR Result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. Same dose.

documents.title: INR Result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range, no change.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed records request with signed release to hospital health information management: discharge summary 1/15-1/22/2026, ICU notes, operative note and discharge summary for L TKA 1/8-1/11/2026. Usual turnaround 2-3 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
4-week follow-up after DVT/PE. Feeling much more herself. No dyspnea walking around the house or the grocery store. Calf swelling gone. Knee bending better with PT, using a cane.

Exam: SpO2 normal on RA. Irregular rhythm, controlled. Lungs clear. Calves symmetric, nontender. L knee incision healed.

A/P: DVT/PE resolving clinically on warfarin; INRs in range - back to every 4 weeks. HIT - avoid heparin, documented. Hospital records not yet received. Return 3 months / with AWV in April.

documents.title: Orthopedic Post-operative Visit
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Joint Replacement Clinic - s/p L TKA 01/08/2026
Allergies: Heparin (HIT), Sulfa
Medications: warfarin, metoprolol succinate, lisinopril, atorvastatin, calcium/vitamin D, acetaminophen, heparin SC

Post-op course complicated by DVT/PE requiring readmission; now on warfarin. Pain improving. Working with outpatient PT.

Exam: incision well healed. ROM 0-105 degrees. Stable. Calf soft.
Radiographs: components well aligned and fixed.

Plan: continue PT for another 4-6 weeks. Return at 1 year.

documents.title: INR Result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. No change. Ortho letter scanned - their med list still shows SC heparin; ours is correct, nothing to do.

reports.text: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response. Normal QRS duration. No acute ST-T abnormality. No change from 06/2025.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.

A hard year with two joint replacements and two clotting complications, but she is walking again without the cane indoors. No falls. Lives alone, managing well; neighbors drove her during recovery. PHQ-9 3 - some low days in February, better now. Health care proxy unchanged.

AF: asymptomatic, rate controlled. ECG unchanged.
DVT/PE: no symptoms.
HIT: allergy in chart; she carries a card.
BP and lipids on yearly labs today.
Joints: R hip and L knee replaced and doing well; the other hip and knee ache now and then.

Exam: irregularly irregular, controlled. Lungs clear. Calves soft, no edema. Healed R hip and L knee incisions.

Prevention: mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy 2029. Vaccines current; flu/COVID in the fall.

Plan: labs today, continue current meds, INR every 4-6 weeks, follow-up in summer.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sandra, your labs look good - kidney and liver tests normal, blood count and platelets normal, cholesterol stable on atorvastatin, INR in range.

documents.title: Records Request - Second Attempt
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Nothing received from 2/10 request. Called hospital HIM - told the request was 'in queue.' Re-faxed request and release. Will check again.

documents.body: INR in range. Continue 5 mg nightly.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 2024 and 2025. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious findings.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up. Back to walking most mornings, about 30 minutes. No palpitations, chest pain, dyspnea, leg swelling or bleeding. Acetaminophen rarely.

Exam: irregular, controlled. Lungs clear. No edema. Both replaced joints with good motion.

A/P: AF on warfarin, HTN, HLD - stable, no changes. Hospital records from January still outstanding despite two requests; front desk to keep after it. INR today, then every 4-6 weeks. Next visit in September.

documents.title: INR Result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Sandra, today's INR is in range - keep taking 5 mg each evening. Next check is with your visit on September 10. Your flu and COVID shots can be given that day too.

documents.body: Thank you! See you then.
